## Changes since 9.3.0-dzbarsky31

- [PR #36](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/36): Include all five gencquery follow-up commits, immediately after the original gencquery commit. Isolate scope-only targets from build actions and conflict checks, preserve complete configured dependency graphs through analysis caching, and keep temporary query graph state local to evaluation. Fix formatter diagnostics, source-file invalidation, path ordering, and configuration identities. The existing 9.3 `config()` syntax is unchanged.
- [PR #44](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/44): Reuse immutable configured attribute maps across Starlark transitions and use weak keys and values for the parsed-flags merge cache. The source PR's partial-analysis benchmark reported mean analysis time of 124.30 to 111.28 seconds; reduced GC contributed to this result.
- [PR #45](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/45): Store custom symlink progress messages only on actions that need them. Default actions use 8 fewer bytes with the measured JVM layout, saving 27.70 MB across 3,462,460 actions.
- [PR #46](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/46): Store the parameter-file type as an integer instead of a per-action enum reference, preserving file contents and action keys. Actions use 8 fewer bytes with the measured JVM layout, saving 7.74 MB across 967,485 actions. This is a retained-memory improvement, not a demonstrated peak-RSS improvement.

### Validation

Fifteen of sixteen targeted test targets passed uncached on Linux remote execution, including gencquery, configured-query, transition, symlink-action, parameter-file-action, and parsed-flags tests. `BazelSkycacheIntegrationTest` passed the new gencquery cases but failed the existing `buildCommand_uploadsFrontierBytesWithUploadMode` count assertion (8 configured targets versus a minimum of 9); the same failure was reproduced on unchanged release 31. The assertion is unchanged. All 21 immutable-release publication checks passed.

### Release publication

Linux and macOS binaries for x86_64 and arm64 are built and version-checked before publication. The immutable release includes SHA-256 checksums and build-provenance attestations. Existing release tags and assets are preserved.
